questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The magnificent nature in the country and great hiking opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: THey have a very diffrent way of examination in New Zealand.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A 7/10. Lots of friendly people to assist me. However, I did not know if a had a place to live on campus before i was there and someone handed me the key.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Free pick up from the airport. 
Orientation days.
An orientation package.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation is a great place to make friends!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Halls and different houses. I lived in a house with three other international students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were offered at the halls. However, I lived in a house with a kitchen and cook by my self.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They do not insulate their houses, so be prepared for a cold time or a big bill.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great for me to live on campus, but the options outside were probably better.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Discussing which courses were relevant for me and how to sign up for them was easy and there was plenty of assistance available.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: During my initial days at the university, I visited the library, where a staff member from the office helped me register for the courses I had identified.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I person talks with the relevant staff

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
10/10
No problems there

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No need to worry, there are helpful individuals around, and things are relatively easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While it may not have been the ideal university for my interest in glaciers and remote sensing, I did discover some relevant courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two BA courses and two mixed BA/MA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style reminded me a lot of my experiences in gymnasium.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Climate Change and Land Use
Enviromental Physics
Physical landscapes - formation and functions
Advanced GIS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Physical landscapes - formation and functions was my favorit. It's a geomorphology course with a focus on New Zealand, featuring numerous field trips. 

A helpful tip is to consult someone in your faculty for course recommendations.

questions.answer: Fees, car rental and gas.

questions.answer: Produce in witer times are expensive!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some were planed by the university, but most done with and by friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of clubs to join and a really nice gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All that you are curius about - it is the best way to meet people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Road trips and hiking! The southern island is beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite simple, with many other international students around, you ended up forming your own little international community.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet them outside of the classrooms in clubs etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not very in to public speaking and a rural energy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and adventurous spirits.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is the smallest university in NZ and it has a rural energy 

Explore the country - it is full of wonders!

Managing time differences can be quite challenging.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's an ideal destination for individuals interested in plants, agriculture, landscape architecture, or business.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to explore the southern island on road trips with friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to a new university and examination system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
